summary: Minutes of a three-day meeting of the Network Graphics Group in July 1973. The group discussed proposals for a protocol to share graphics across the network, including an alternative design handed out to attendees to read before the following day's discussion.

plainLanguage.summary: These minutes record a Network Graphics Group meeting about graphics over the ARPANET. Participants compared experiments and discussed how a shared graphics system might work.

questions: what problems did early graphics experiments have
subtitle: Minutes of discussions and experiments at a Network Graphics Group meeting.

tldr.problem: The Network Graphics Group discussed how computers might share graphics over the network and what a graphics protocol should support.
tldr.mechanism: The minutes record experiment reports and discussions of display segments, connections, input, and protocol options.
tldr.outcome: Participants favored a transformed-segmented scheme for further attention and continued to regard the protocol as experimental.

sections.title: Network Graphics Experiments
sections.content:
The minutes cover a Network Graphics Group meeting held July 15-17, 1973. Participants described graphics experiments, including one that found performance unacceptable over a 300 baud connection and another that experienced delays of up to 20 seconds.

An aircraft flight simulator report said at least 5 updates per second were needed for an adequate feeling of control.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants reported both successful and difficult graphics experiments. Some faced slow connections or long delays, while one simulator needed frequent updates.

sections.title: Display Data and Protocol Choices
sections.content:
The group discussed a move from protocol levels to negotiable options. It agreed to focus on a simpler transformed-segmented scheme and delay consideration of a hierarchically structured scheme until another meeting.

The minutes describe segments that can be created, replaced, or deleted, and an end-batch-of-updates command so multiple display changes can take effect together.
sections.plainLanguage: The group favored negotiable options over fixed levels and chose to focus on a simpler segmented display approach. Updates could be applied together at the end of a batch.

sections.title: Connections, Input, and Experimental Status
sections.content:
Participants discussed using TELNET and whether graphics should use a second connection pair or share one connection; the number of connections would be negotiated over TELNET. They also discussed input devices and agreed that a server must enable them before the using host supplies input.

The minutes say the protocol was still experimental and describe required, optional, and experimental feature categories.
sections.plainLanguage: The group discussed how graphics data and input would move between hosts. The proposed protocol remained experimental, with features divided into required, optional, and experimental groups.
